# Best rechargeable AA batteries

For most people, buy low-self-discharge NiMH cells: Panasonic Eneloop, Eneloop Pro, or the IKEA LADDA equivalent. Which one fits depends on your device.

## My picks

**Best overall for high-drain devices (flashes, cameras, controllers): Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA**
- Digital Camera World's reviewer has used them for years with "100 per cent reliability." Specs: 2,600 mAh, 85% charge after 1 year, about 500 recharges, and an operating range of -4° to 122°F. [Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)
- The tradeoff is higher price and fewer cycles than standard Eneloop. GearLab lists a 4-pack at $17.99. [GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)
- Buy: the [Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) links to Adorama, Amazon, and Newegg. It showed Amazon prices of about $21.89 to $34.87, so compare before buying.

**Best value: IKEA LADDA**
- Charge-Test found the 2450 mAh LADDA cells measured about 2,450 mAh at low load and 2,348 mAh at 1A, close to Eneloop Pro. The tester concluded they're still "Eneloop-class cells at budget prices." [Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)
- The IKEA US page I have lists the 1900 mAh version at $9.99 for 4. [Buy at IKEA](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/) The 1900 mAh cell is the Eneloop-standard equivalent and is good for everyday devices.
- The 2450 mAh version is the better match for high-drain use. GearLab quotes $7.99 in-store, but Charge-Test's prices are in euros, and I couldn't confirm US availability or pricing for the 2450 model. Check your local IKEA.

**Best for bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO AA, 2,800 mAh, 20-pack**
- $42.99 (about $2.15 per cell), verified 2026-10-21. Rated for 1,200 cycles and 85% charge after 1 year. Smaller packs are also available (4 for $11.99, 8 for $21.99). [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack)
- [Buy at Tenergy's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.
- These figures come from the manufacturer, and I found no independent test of this model. Return shipping is on you, and the warranty is unclear (12 months on the product page, 90 days on Tenergy's warranty page).

## Cautions
- **Devices that need 1.5V:** NiMH cells run at 1.2V. Digital Camera World recommends the [EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries) for these.
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity:** Opinions are split. GearLab recommends it for low-drain items like remotes and clocks. Two Frame & Focal articles report poor performance under load and after a year of use, but their claims are inconsistent with each other and some are implausible (such as zinc dendrites in NiMH cells), so I'd treat them with caution.
- **Charger:** You'll need a decent NiMH charger. IKEA sells one with the LADDA cells for $8.99.

If you tell me what you're powering (camera flash, controllers, remotes, etc.), I can narrow this to one pick.
